subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what guarantee should it make across top-level navigations, redirects, subframes/subresources, and proxy-routed browser profiles?
rationale: The request adds security-sensitive public config semantics that current SSRF hostname allowlists do not define, so automation should not choose the permanent browser policy boundary.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped deny/warn semantics before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Make the generic egress-firewall direction own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser-specific behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable denylist and document or surface best-effort bot-block warnings that do not claim to be a security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped deny/warn semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across the browser config, docs, and navigation security-policy surface.
